proof.text: Choose a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $K_0$ and a functor equivalence $e:K_0\to K$; enlarge the containing universe if needed. Put $p:\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$ for the terminal functor. By the absolute-terminal identification, $p$ is an inner fibration and a diagram is a $p$-colimit diagram exactly when its cocone is colimiting. Apply the equivalence-reindexing clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] to $q$ and $e$. It gives that $q_0=q\,e^{\triangleright}:K_0^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ is colimiting, with the boundary and all higher coherent data obtained by the specified precomposition.

proof.text: Apply the same two nodes to the terminal functor $Z\to\Delta^0$, the equivalence $e:K_0\to K$, and the particular cocone $Hq$ indexed by $K$. The absolute-terminal identification turns the relative assertion into ordinary colimitingness, while equivalence-reindexing says that $Hq$ is colimiting if and only if $(Hq)e^{\triangleright}=Hq_0$ is. Since the latter was proved in Step 2, the original specified image cocone $Hq$ itself is colimiting; no replacement cocone or new apex is chosen.

title: Small-colimit preservation extends to essentially small canonical cocones
statement: Use coherent functors, equivalences and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and join cocones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$, with all categories and cocones below in a sufficiently large containing universe. Here, for a diagram $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ into a quasicategory $\mathcal C$ with $f=q|_K$ and apex $x=q(*)$, its cocone is the coherent transformation $f\to\Delta_Kx$ obtained by precomposing $q$ with the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ that keeps the vertices labelled $0$ in $K$ and sends the vertices labelled $1$ to the cone point; $q$ is called colimiting when this cocone is initial in the coherent cocone category. Let $\mathcal C,Z$ be quasicategories, and let $H:\mathcal C\to Z$ preserve all $\mathcal U$-small colimits, meaning that it sends every colimiting coherent cocone with $\mathcal U$-small simplicial indexing set to a colimiting cocone. Let $K$ be a quasicategory equivalent to a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory, and let $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ be a specified colimiting cocone. Then the entire image cocone $Hq:K^{\triangleright}\to Z$ is colimiting, with its given boundary, apex and higher coherent simplices. No existence of other colimits in $\mathcal C$ or $Z$ is required. In particular, the conclusion concerns the specified image cocone itself, rather than a separately chosen colimit of a small equivalent diagram.
